subject: economics
title: Labour Market Exam Stretch
welcome_lead: The government wants policy advice. Match the right intervention to each unemployment type and evaluate trade-offs.
meta_desc: GCSE Economics exam-style adventure on unemployment: policy evaluation, costs of joblessness and structural challenges.
final_note: Labour market mastered. Time for economic growth!

concepts.def: Long-term unemployment leads to lost skills.
Policies to push people into work (training).
Policy boosting AD to cut cyclical unemployment.
National Minimum Wage — legal pay floor.

walkthroughs.body_html: Cyclical → boost AD (cut taxes, lower rates). Structural → retraining, regional grants. Frictional → better job-matching websites. Seasonal → diversify regional economy. The exam loves a 'match the policy' question.

For individuals: lost income, mental health, skill atrophy. For government: more welfare, less tax. For economy: lower output (below potential GDP), wasted resources. For society: rising inequality and crime. Top-band answers list multiple stakeholders.
Evaluate by: time (training takes years), cost (cuts may worsen things), magnitude, side-effects (NMW may price low-skilled out). Conclude with a justified judgement on the best policy mix.

mcqs.q: Which policy best tackles STRUCTURAL unemployment?
options: Cutting interest rates
Funding retraining for displaced workers
Raising VAT
Reducing the minimum wage

mcqs.q: Long-term unemployment causing permanent skill loss is called?
options: Cyclical effect
Hysteresis
Friction
Underemployment

mcqs.q: What is the difference between a shift in demand and a movement along the demand curve?
options: Demand always falls when supply increases.
Inflation is when the economy grows too fast.
A movement along the curve is caused by a change in price; a shift of the whole curve is caused by changes in other factors (income, tastes, substitute prices).
A change in price shifts the demand curve.
A sustained rise in the general price level over time — reducing the purchasing power of money. Measured by the percentage change in a price index.
Inflation is when prices are high.
Supply shifts only when consumers want more.
Inflation is when the economy grows too fast.

mcqs.q: What causes the supply curve to shift?
options: Supply shifts only when consumers want more.
When demand rises, the supply curve shifts right to meet it.
Demand always falls when supply increases.
Changes in production costs, technology, taxes/subsidies, number of producers, expectations — anything affecting supply other than the good's own price.
